comment: States the visual QA tour walks, in the order a player meets them. Adding a state is a JSON entry, not a new function. 'at_seconds' is wall time since the client connected; the tour walks the list in order and never goes backwards. 'camera' picks a pose: follow, overview, or first_person. 'note' is what the critic should be looking at, and is copied into the manifest beside the still.

states.name: boot_menu
states.note: First thing anyone sees. Option text legible, nothing clipped, the focused option obvious without reading it.

states.name: warmup_spectator
states.note: Warmup bumper and roster. Does the chrome tell you the round has not started without a sentence of text.

states.name: arena_overview
states.note: The map read from above. Cover legible, lanes readable, no flat untextured ground.

states.name: combat_follow
states.note: A fight in progress. Muzzle flash, tracer, hit feedback. This is the effects bar: does a shot look like it hit something.

states.name: hud_first_person
states.note: HUD density. Count the words on screen. Weapon identifiable by silhouette, health and armour readable as shape not sentence.

states.name: hud_with_pickup
states.note: A pickup prompt in view. Does the prompt add one icon or one more block of text.

states.name: shot_effects
states.note: Eight consecutive frames from pulling the trigger. Muzzle flash, tracer, impact, hit feedback. A still at a fixed second never catches a sixty millisecond effect, so this is the only place effects can be judged.

states.name: shot_effects_third_person
states.note: The same trigger pull watched from outside. The muzzle flash lives on the fighter's pawn, so this is where it shows; compare with the first-person strip above.

states.name: compliance_pressure
states.note: The compliance beat. Pressure should read as colour and motion, not a banner.

states.name: killfeed_scoreboard
states.note: Killfeed and score. The one place text is allowed. Check it is not competing with the crosshair.
